title: Supplier Servicing, Repair Loaners and Manufacturer Warranties in Durable Medical Equipment Rentals
content:
Suppliers furnishing Durable Medical Equipment Rentals items are bound by the servicing, loaner and warranty terms of the item's payment class. Maintenance and servicing is paid, where the class allows it, after the cap or after a purchase, at the class's interval between payable visits.

## Supplier obligations and payable servicing by class

| Payment class | Maintenance and servicing paid after the cap or purchase | Months between payable maintenance and servicing visits | Supplier must provide a loaner while owned equipment is repaired | Supplier must pass on the manufacturer warranty on purchased or owned items |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inexpensive or Routinely Purchased Equipment | No | 0 (not payable) | No | Yes |
| Capped Rental Equipment | Yes | 6 | Yes | Yes |
| Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Equipment | Yes | 6 | Yes | Yes |
| Power Mobility Device | Yes | 6 | Yes | Yes |
| Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment | No | 0 (not payable) | Yes | Yes |
| Frequently Serviced Equipment | No | 0 (not payable) | Yes | Yes |
| Customized Equipment | Yes | 6 | Yes | Yes |

An interval of 0 means maintenance and servicing visits are not payable in that class.

## Notes to the table

1. Payable servicing after the cap or purchase, one payable visit every 6 months, applies to Capped Rental Equipment, Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Equipment, Power Mobility Device and Customized Equipment.
2. Inexpensive or Routinely Purchased Equipment, Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment and Frequently Serviced Equipment have no payable maintenance and servicing after the cap or purchase.
3. A loaner while owned equipment is under repair is owed in every class except Inexpensive or Routinely Purchased Equipment.
4. The manufacturer warranty on purchased or owned items is passed on by the supplier in all seven classes.

### Hypothetical illustration

A hypothetical owned Power Mobility Device needing repair: the class requires the supplier to provide a loaner while it is repaired, and payable maintenance and servicing visits fall 6 months apart. A hypothetical owned walker in Inexpensive or Routinely Purchased Equipment: no loaner is owed during repair and no maintenance and servicing visit is payable, while the manufacturer warranty is still passed on.
